issue.title: Continue #759 after #771: complete automated CST translation, runtime parity and JavaScript-first CI
issue.body:
Continue #759 after the meaningful checkpoint in #771 (following merged #761). The user explicitly requested prompt checkpoint merge and a separate issue preserving **all** remaining requirements. This rollover does not certify full translation, runtime parity or a green JavaScript gate. Keep #759 open.

## Accepted checkpoint and evidence

PR #771 is now **merged** at `eb2dad1c0a18394dc1aad46413e11401e74eb502` (final PR head `5c3354948dc9186a22267d576d62b950cf41407d`). GitHub confirmed the merge at `2026-10-21T18:44:29Z`. The final-head checks were still queued when the user-authorized meaningful checkpoint merged; they are not represented as green.

The completed source checkpoint is `2018b7d021d5f601afbcd4394a69268345f6aa59`; the rollover adds documentation only. It contains physical `rust/src`, `js/src` and `ts/src` trees, an extensible two-phase substitution pipeline, serialized/reparsed CST boundaries, receiving-source history repairs, complete source-equation transactions, strict physical-source fixture refresh, bounded owned-field storage proposals and same-SHA JavaScript-before-Rust workflow audits.

Qualified complete-file receiving batches at that checkpoint:

- Source-equation/Core effects/formatting/text: 41 cases across six complete files pass in both Node and Bun under original deadlines.
- Private DATA/source-equation history: 34 cases across six complete files pass in both engines under original deadlines.
- Static-universe and workflow policy controls: 38 cases across two complete files pass in both engines. The installed current fixture contains 865 Rust/Cargo inputs while retaining the original 806/808 historical universes.
- Additional receiving batches and exact limitations are documented under `docs/development/`. These overlapping batches are not an aggregate whole-suite result or an executable-coverage gain.

The last fully collected remote head, `c6bed6215e157de4381e39e04b4cb1ef02720384`, has 132 terminal checks: 30 success, 40 failure, 20 cancelled and 42 skipped. All 60 failed/cancelled complete streams were retained and verified locally. Rust jobs did not unlock. Later local repairs require fresh remote results; cancellation, skipped work and missing results remain unqualified.

The last measured executable production baseline is **155/2,567 functions (6.04%)** against an older 847-source inventory. It is not a current percentage for the newer 865-input fixture. The recorded 441 parity gaps (2 implemented, 151 partial, 290 unsupported) and `runtimeParity: false` remain open until a fresh complete census proves otherwise. Candidate counts, preserved source and library API declarations do not count as executable application coverage.

## First repair batch: qualify the actual complete path

- [ ] Collect every result/log from the final #771 head and its merge SHA before publishing another coordinated repair batch. Do not cancel active CI or push fix-by-fix. Record the exact SHA, compiler versions and resource receipts.
- [ ] Finish canonical and neutral/Unix/Windows full-corpus generation, all owned-definition outputs, strict TypeScript **5.9.3**, deterministic freshness, reverse regeneration and strict parity. The current full compiler bank/export must be rebuilt and qualified from current inputs; an older exported snapshot is not current evidence.
- [ ] Repair missing neutral output trees, stale generated inventories, incomplete reverse runs and full profile-matrix memory failures. Preserve original heap, aggregate RSS, disk, evidence and case limits. No `continue-on-error`, skipped-as-green or reduced corpus workaround.
- [ ] Optimize the shared causes of original deadlines: Bun derive-helper provider/getter and response-affinity cases retain their default 5,000 ms limits; static-source lifecycle and retained-storage Node CLI retain 60,000 ms; Core child retains 12,500 ms; CatalogRecord retains 60,000 ms. Run the complete original files in both engines. A synchronous late TAP pass remains red.
- [ ] Qualify actual full native retained-storage generation. Previous unchanged full-generation OOMs remain failures; passing storage controls does not prove the complete producer fits. Preserve complete CSV original receiving cases and every other unrun consumer.
- [ ] Complete all eight mandatory JavaScript stages for the **same immutable SHA**, then run all applicable Rust checks in CI and treat Rust failures as fatal. Do not run any Rust tool locally.

## Increase useful translation coverage in large shared steps

- [ ] Rank current production refusals by the actual functions a shared rule can unlock. Re-census after each qualified batch. The older worklist includes outer module-binding masking, format expansion, mutable references, generic state, scoped `matches!`, standard-library imports and shadowed string bindings; those counts are diagnostic priorities, not proven coverage gains.
- [ ] Finish owner-qualified namespace/import/producer closure and associated receiver evidence. Preserve unknown/unresolved ownership refusals; a familiar spelling, token-origin flag, metadata object or CST reconstruction never grants semantic authority.
- [ ] Extend checked language rules for frequently occurring control flow, patterns, ownership/borrowing, calls, data layouts, formatting and library operations using independent positive, negative and boundary fixtures.
- [ ] Use matching Rust/JavaScript/TypeScript compatibility-core abstractions where this allows qualified application usages to translate directly. Intentionally untranslated internals must remain explicitly listed and behaviorally tested. Do not count those internals as translated.
- [ ] Review preserved namespace, formatting and enclosing-owner source proposals before integration. Some drafts were already partially received: compare exact current before/after sources instead of blindly applying old patches. Unsealed or unrun drafts do not increase coverage.
- [ ] Revisit the parked metadata-copy optimization only after preserving native error behavior, callback operations, source authentication and both engines' stack observations. Its 30-case Node batch passes; Bun fails actual native-error-message equality and a stack control. The prototype was excluded from #771. CPU sampling identified metadata copying/hashing as a hotspot; no qualified end-to-end speed gain is claimed for that prototype.

## Carry forward every requirement of #759

1. [ ] **Case study and evidence:** complete the source-pinned timeline, requirement-to-change/check mapping, root causes and measured comparisons under `docs/case-studies/issue-759`. Preserve complete compressed logs/data, distinguish missing evidence from established causes, add bounded verbose diagnostics where needed, and review applicable primary sources and existing components. Reuse the best actual approaches from formal-ai#1188, meta-language#201 and relative-meta-logic while retaining their licenses, versions and limits.
2. [ ] **Native JavaScript Router with full runtime parity:** cover configuration, routing, cooldowns, accounts/tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints, CLI and every documented operation in Node 20+ and Bun. Keep the existing JavaScript wrapper/downstream contract working. Require independent shared fixtures/goldens and a feature manifest/checker for both implementations; a binary wrapper or consistent inventory alone is insufficient.
3. [ ] **Fully automated bidirectional synchronization:** complete Rust → serialized/reparsed CST/meta → JavaScript/TypeScript and JavaScript → serialized/reparsed CST/meta → Rust/TypeScript. Develop covered behavior in JavaScript first. Regenerate and diff complete outputs in CI. Retain explicit unsupported constructs and small native-library boundaries until implemented; no manual generated-body repairs or source-preservation-as-execution claims.
4. [ ] **Bulk drafting and one publisher:** keep coherent batches, a complete failure set and reviewable commits at least every six hours during active work. The user's latest instruction is for the coordinator to work alone after workers finish; no new workers without renewed authorization. Preserve the reusable multi-worker/single-publisher workflow and verify/report the required orchestration support in hive-mind. Standing push authorization does not require another approval question.
5. [ ] **Minimal local load:** JavaScript diagnostics locally; **no local Cargo, rustc, rustfmt, Clippy, rust-script or Rust-backed hooks** for this task. One heavy workload at a time, existing dependencies/worktrees, bounded compressed evidence, measured optimization before retries, and cleanup restricted to identified task-owned inactive files. No new across-invocation source/hash/owner/verdict/encoded-result caches.
6. [ ] **JavaScript-before-Rust everywhere:** audit every entry/reusable/release/supplemental workflow, path filter, skipped/cancelled result, SHA join and concurrency setting. Require all eight JavaScript stages before Rust for the same SHA and require the fatal Rust checks afterward. Verify actual required-check/branch-rule behavior. Supplemental draft selection never converts skipped jobs to success or waives the main gate.
7. [ ] **Measure results:** report reproducible before/after pushes per PR, all green/failed/cancelled runs, actual CI minutes, time to first complete green run and peak local RSS/disk. Distinguish sampled diagnostics, isolated operations and whole-workload observations; do not invent cost or coverage savings.
8. [ ] **Reusable adoption:** finish export and receiving-repository qualification of the compiler, source-preparation tools, CST extension, compatibility core, gates, manifests and contribution guidance. Apply the qualified standard to the Rust and JavaScript pipeline templates and hive-mind guidance; verify/open deduplicated adoption issues in formal-ai, meta-language, relative-meta-logic, link-cli, links-notation, start and calculator with links to #759 and this issue.
9. [ ] **Cross-repository audit:** verify previously completed reports and file any still-missing reproducible issues in the affected repositories. Cover native JS parity, translation/freshness, gate bypasses, cancelled CI, Rust resource policies, agent rules, pinned actions, release/publish, links/security checks and guards, recurring default-branch defects and stale PRs. Include concrete evidence, a minimal reproduction, workarounds and testable fixes; avoid duplicate reports or unqualified upstream blame.

## Translation and completion contract

- All translation and automated source preparation use ordered substitution rules: a reusable **language** sequence followed by a Router **repository** sequence. Extend those lists or compose pipelines for further layers. Keep CST transport, checked semantic representations and native syntax/owner/type/effect validation independent. Preserve complete source inverses and exact installed-producer freshness.
- Keep physical `./js/src`, `./ts/src` and `./rust/src`. Bulk-draft the full requirement list through automation, repair shared rules, and regenerate targets rather than patching generated bodies.
- Preserve original whole test files, callbacks, refusal sets and deadlines in Node and Bun. Add Rust edge-case test source for overflow, empty values, Unicode, malformed input, ordering and errors where relevant; report it as unrun until gated CI executes it.
- Keep `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, JavaScript-first guidance, the continuation ledger and requirement/check records aligned. Use “links network” terminology and keep files below 1,000 lines.
- Completion requires a fresh actual production census, complete native runtime parity, complete bidirectional output freshness, current receiving export qualification, all eight same-SHA JavaScript stages and applicable gated Rust CI. Preserve every failed and unrun obligation until then. A bulk draft, merged checkpoint or green subset is not 100% completion.

References: #759, #761, #771; [formal-ai#1188](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1188), [meta-language#201](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/201), [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic). Implementation contracts and receiving evidence: `docs/development/translation-rule-api.md`, `translation-rules.md`, `compatibility-core.md`, `javascript-first.md`, `concrete-source-equations.md`, `strict-static-source-refresh.md`, `current-receiving-source-history.md` and `native-output-text-retention.md`.

## Continuation PR #775

Development continues in #775 at `f54a999da6f9b7c5dbf3870b38d8ab70779d7fb2`. The [throughput plan](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/f54a999da6f9b7c5dbf3870b38d8ab70779d7fb2/docs/development/translation-throughput-plan.md) prioritizes shared owned-operation families, both translation directions and whole executable production callers. The first batch fixes shared Bun syntax verification, derives the actual private metadata dispatcher through both CST rule phases, and retains complete prior CI/local receiving evidence. Node passes 39/39 selected cases; Bun passes 37/39, including all 30 metadata and five typed-target controls. Two original derive cases still exceed their unchanged 5,000 ms defaults. Full generation, strict parity, reverse/export freshness and the complete gate remain unqualified; no new application coverage or controlled speed gain is claimed. No local Rust tool ran.
